_source: Fault Lines (11K subs), Florida Learjet crash reconstructed in 3D, 1.94M views, 10:08. Built-in browser 2026-11-20: 0-65 s played with the audio probe (frames every 5-10 s), then 175, 275, 316, 335, 352, 362/372 (burst at the dive), 405, 456, 522, 590 s; transcript panel counted (1,376 words, ~140 wpm; never copied). SAMPLED. Our own descriptions.

hook.firstFrame: a clean white 3D business jet above sunlit clouds; top-left mono tag '3D RECONSTRUCTION - NOT ACTUAL FOOTAGE'; a crest logo bottom-right
hook.firstLine: A business jet cruising high, bound for the Bahamas.

shots.picture: white 3D jet over clouds, slow orbit
3D flight path as a white ribbon over a dark navy grid, an orange curtain to the ground; mono callouts at cruise, the turn and impact
camera orbits the same path; captions bold white, one word in blue
slow push on the jet; red pill top-right asking to subscribe
low-poly town from above: grey box houses, dot trees, a smoke column, a white ring on the road at the crash site
fact card on dark navy with drifting dust: orange mono labels, white values appear line by line
jet at cruise, lower-left label with an orange bar: altitude and speed, as reported
comparison bars: a small blue square for a normal descent, a long red bar for this jet; status chip 'as reported, not yet verified'
centred serif title over the darkened 3D jet: how a spiral dive works, in general
front-view physics diagram: wing line, green lift arrow tilting, red side force; a yellow mono cause chain at the bottom
banked jet lost in grey cloud, label 'no horizon in cloud'
dip to near-black while the dive is described
storm cross-section: altitude axis, red up arrows, blue down arrows, plane icon at cruise height; 'general principle' chip
debris-pattern diagram: compact crater cluster vs wide spread
real licensed photo of the aircraft type, credit tag top-left in mono
end card: wordmark with a red slash, red subscribe button, a promise line

lines.gist: a business jet at cruise, heading for the islands
a minute later it hit a road almost vertically; nine aboard, none lived
we rebuild the last minutes in 3D from tracking data, radio and weather
early subscribe ask, framed around the work the rebuild took
what is new since the first reports: aircraft, age, owner
the flight from take-off to cruise, rebuilt step by step
the descent rate compared with a normal approach
how a spiral dive and a storm can each bring a jet down, in general
what the wreckage and the investigation can and cannot show
known, unknown, condolences, a promise to rebuild with the official report

ending.cta: subscribe; the flight will be rebuilt again with the official report
ending.lastFrame: wordmark, red subscribe button, promise line

whyItWorks: The whole story in the first 17 s: cruise, the minute, the impact, the toll, then the method (rebuilt from tracking data).
The flight path is the hero: a 3D ribbon over a grid with mono callouts at each event, revisited from new angles.
Honesty labels on every picture (reconstruction, illustrative path, as reported, general principle) build trust.
A ten-chapter list makes 10 minutes feel like a run of short answers.
